  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: §25.B’s prohibition on polls the model sets up “on your own initiative” depends on the model reliably identifying its own initiative, with no enforcement mechanism.
  WHY: The enforcement boundary is unchanged from existing prose-only rules, and the carve-out has concrete stopping rules and scope limits.
- CLAUDE.md:1566-1601 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: §25.B and §25.C do not establish whether a user-requested scheduled status check may push review-blocked fixes, run the in-workflow resolver, dispatch a `force_rb_judge` round, or trigger an autofix iteration.
  WHY: “Under plain §12” could authorize those actions on every scheduled check, although the §25.B carve-out was meant to be narrower than the banned poll.
- CLAUDE.md:1548, 1550-1555 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The §25 heading uses “watching” while the introduction describes the rule as subscribing and acting on PR activity unprompted.
  WHY: A future reader could interpret the heading as banning any scheduled look at a PR, reintroducing the interpretation §25 just relaxed.
- CLAUDE.md:1587-1601 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: §25.C permits recurring scheduled status checks without a documented deterministic gate, kill switch, or per-tick log path.
  WHY: The documented `pr_watch_guard.py` only covers `subscribe_pr_activity` calls, so a `send_later`-driven check is invisible to that guard.
- CLAUDE.md:1553–1555 and 1594–1601 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The introduction says §25 “holds even when the user asks for PR watching,” while §25.C permits a user-requested scheduled PR status check.
  WHY: The conflicting instruction can cause a session to refuse a scheduled check the user explicitly requested, defeating the change’s stated purpose.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:382, 1362 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The provided CI result reports 5 failed tests and 171 passed in `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`; the aggregate `lint` check consequently fails.
  WHY: The test job exits non-zero, so the aggregate CI check fails and blocks a green PR check. The supplied log tail does not identify the failing test names or map them to this documentation diff.

The PR diff shows only `CLAUDE.md` (4 hunks in §25) and `changelog.d/6202-claude-md-25-scheduled-status-checks.md`. `git diff --stat` confirms the two-file scope. The "Unchanged" claim is therefore accurate as far as the diff shows, but the PR description does not demonstrate that `pr_watch_guard.py` and `.claude/settings.json` still pass their wiring tests under the new §25 prose — `tests/test_pr_watch_guard.py` includes assertions on `is_subscribe_tool`, the `SETTINGS_MATCHER`, and `test_claude_md_documents_the_rule`, none of which are exercised by the prose-only diff. The PR description's "70 passed" line only names `tests/test_pr_watch_guard.py` and `tests/test_claude_md_section_numbers.py`; it does not assert anything about the other 5 tests in the `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` job that the PR head SHA `d7a7797bff6786a05c2fb3348d654c8731b46ba4` failed (`5 failed, 171 passed in 6.84s`, see `pr_check_runs_context.txt` failed[1].log_tail).

  expected_change_site: `tests/test_pr_watch_guard.py` and `tests/test_claude_md_section_numbers.py`
  confidence=[5]

  EVIDENCE: The PR head SHA fails the `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` CI job with 5 failures and 171 passes. The captured 16 KB log tail (`pr_check_runs_context.txt`, `failed[1].log_tail`) does not name the failing tests — it shows source code from `pr_merge_status_guard.py` being printed during test execution, but the test names and assertion errors are not in the visible window. The PR's test claim is restricted to two test files (the §25-specific ones) and does not cover the 5 failing tests in the same job; reviewers and operators reading the description cannot tell whether those 5 failures are pre-existing on `main`, introduced by the PR, or surface only on this PR head SHA. The aggregate `lint` job also fails (`pr_check_runs_context.txt`, `failed[0]`, exit code 1, "CI jobs that did not succeed: tests-hooks-and-orchestrator").

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- CLAUDE.md:1582-1585 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: §25.B's new prohibition bans polls the model sets up "on your own initiative" — phrasing that relies on the model self-identifying initiative, which is an implicit capability gate with no enforcement mechanism.
  WHY: The model's self-assessment of its own initiative is unreliable and untestable. Every other constraint in §25 is enforceable by a hook (`pr_watch_guard.py`) or a deterministic rule; this one is enforced only by the model's own classification of whether it was "asked for" or "on its own initiative." However, this is a pre-existing architectural limitation of CLAUDE.md rules — §2's "Always-On Ask-First Mode" and §0's "Prime Directive" are only enforced by the model reading them, not by hooks. The change does not introduce a new class of gap; it narrows an existing prohibition by adding a carve-out whose enforcement boundary is unchanged. The carve-out has concrete stopping rules ("Stop it when the PR merges or closes, or when the user says to stop") and explicit scope ("acts only within what the user asked for, under plain §12").

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- CLAUDE.md:1566-1572 (§25.A), 1574-1585 (§25.B), 1587-1601 (§25.C) | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: §25.C allows a "scheduled status check" that "reads the PR's state, CI, and reviews, and acts only within what the user asked for, under plain §12", and §25.B bans only "a poll of a PR's CI or review activity that the user did not ask for". The two paragraphs together introduce a partial overlap that is not resolved: §25.B names a poll of "CI or review activity" as the thing the user must ask for, while §25.A's parenthetical restricts the fix path to "a scheduled status check they asked for, §25.C". A session that has been asked to "check hourly and get these PRs to completion" can interpret that request as license to take action under §12.A (which authorizes "direct chat request" fixes); §25.C's "acts only within what the user asked for, under plain §12" then endorses that reading instead of constraining it. The new §25 prose does not say whether the scheduled check may also push review-blocked fixes, run the in-workflow resolver, dispatch a `force_rb_judge` round, or trigger an autofix iteration — §12 covers all of that, and the "under plain §12" clause keeps every one of those paths reachable.
  WHY: A user-requested scheduled check could in principle invoke every §12.B category on every tick, because §25.C's "under plain §12" clause explicitly routes through §12 rather than constraining it. The §25.B carve-out for "scheduled status checks" was meant to be narrower than the banned poll; the wording does not establish that.
- CLAUDE.md: line 1548 (heading) versus lines 1550-1555 (intro) | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The §25 heading still reads "PR Watching Is Disabled (MANDATORY)" while the intro paragraph now defines the rule as "never subscribe to a pull request's activity ... never act on a PR's CI or review activity unprompted". The two parts use different operative verbs ("watching" vs "subscribe"), and §25.A's parenthetical adds a third ("scheduled status check"). `tests/test_pr_watch_guard.py:251` pins the heading verbatim and continues to pass; `tests/test_pr_watch_guard.py:264` pins the §12.G "INACTIVE — superseded by §25" string and continues to pass; the changelog fragment also still names §25 in §25's voice. So the strings the tests pin are intact, but the rule itself is now expressed in two verbs, and a reader (or future prose edit) can read the heading and miss that "watching" has been narrowed to "subscribing + acting on CI/review activity unprompted".
  WHY: A reviewer of a future change could read the heading "PR Watching Is Disabled" and conclude that any scheduled look at a PR (a routine poll, a daily CI dig, a watchlist summary) is banned, reintroducing the exact reading §25 just relaxed. The new intro only lives at the top of §25; the heading is the dominant signal in any index or grep hit on "watch".
